prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system (automatic control, manual intervention); boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Aliases: Ironwood=River Intake Pump Station (start permissives: suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips; lost permissive→alarm/stop; maintenance release after isolations tagged/verified/logged). Lantern=SCADA Historian Server (trends, doses, analyzers, filters, washes, lab times; backwash recovery data). Marigold=Coagulant Dosing Skid (sends Alum Batch Ticket on new lot; receives Jar Test Photograph Set; adjusts within approved limits; shall hold last operator-approved dose if quality data inconsistent/unavailable). Cobalt=North Filter Gallery (may stagger washes). Sparrow=Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (sends Jar Test Photograph Set). Quarry=Maintenance Planner (informed of repeated solids-handling problems). Juniper=High Service Pump Header (produces Pump Bearing Vibration Clip; lead/lag, no short cycling, avoids pressure swings in recovery; first indication of demand via discharge pressure, flow, pump status). Falcon=Distribution Dispatcher (notified before header changes or treatment changes affecting North/South Distribution Pressure Station reserves; watches sustained zone deviations; reports breaks/complaints). Elements: Raw Water Screen Channel (Rake Torque Snapshot→Maintenance Planner); South Filter Gallery (Filter Run Exception Note→Chief Operator); Clearwell Level Controller (sends Clearwell Diver Entry Permit; low interlock, high alarm) monitored with Chlorine Contact Basin; Backwash Recovery Tank (return after settling/clarity check, else held); North Distribution Pressure Station (separate zone: suction/discharge pressure, pump availability, comms); South Distribution Pressure Station (starts lead booster when discharge below start band for delay). Actors: Chief Operator (produces Backwash Solids Manifest after verified solids event), Duty Engineer, Laboratory Technician (Sample Chain Slip), Chemical Supplier Driver (Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log). Item: Chlorine Residual Alarm (during filtration upset = finished-water protection issue). Modes: Automatic; Manual (only if automatic unavailable, reason stated); Storm Intake Mode; Upset classes by Chief Operator: advisory (monitor), controlled (operator-directed change), critical (protect water; notify Duty Engineer if automatic can't hold envelope). Resume normal: stable quality, residuals done, alarms cleared, Chief Operator closes. Compare pressure with reservoir/pump/field trends before setpoint

New part:
S181: When a distribution station is in automatic operation, local controls are expected to sequence pumps within approved limits and report abnormal starts, failures, or valve positions to the control system.
S182: When a distribution station is in local or manual operation, the Distribution Dispatcher records the reason, the expected duration, and the field contact responsible for the change.
S183: The Clearwell Level Controller is checked before large distribution adjustments so that high service pumping does not create avoidable level instability.
S184: The Chief Operator may direct a conservative pumping posture during unusual demand, main repair activity, or recovery from a treatment upset.
S185: The Duty Engineer reviews persistent low-pressure complaints, repeated station alarms, or mismatches between observed pressure and modeled expectations.
S186: Cobalt shall provide a reliable filter service status indication before the control room treats increased distribution demand as available finished-water capacity.
S187: Sparrow records incoming distribution check samples with the pressure zone, collection point, and time needed for control-room review.
S188: The SCADA Historian Server uses the Sample Chain Slip to associate distribution water-quality entries with the operating period shown in the electronic log.
S189: The Distribution Dispatcher sends the Pressure Zone Handoff Card after verifying current pressure-zone setpoints, active alarms, and open field work.
S190: Shift handoff includes any disabled alarms, temporary operating limits, pending station inspections, and customer complaint trends that may affect dispatch decisions.
S191: If communication to a distribution station is lost, the control room assumes the last confirmed operating mode remains in effect until field verification or telemetry restoration proves otherwise.
S192: Field crews notify the control room before opening or closing major distribution valves so that pressure changes can be distinguished from pump or instrumentation problems.
S193: The Distribution Dispatcher coordinates planned hydrant flushing, valve exercising, and main isolation work with pumping schedules to limit avoidable pressure swings.
S194: When a Chlorine Residual Alarm is active, distribution pressure decisions remain coordinated with water-quality response actions rather than being treated as a purely hydraulic issue.
S195: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench provides analytical status through normal plant reporting channels, and the control room uses that status to interpret pressure-zone complaints involving taste, odor, or disinfectant concerns.
S196: The SCADA Historian Server retains pressure, flow, pump status, and alarm data needed to reconstruct dispatch decisions after an event.
S197: During Storm Intake Mode, the Distribution Dispatcher avoids unnecessary zone changes unless demand, storage, or public-safety conditions require action.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
